items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: At the same time you sit down and do a duo thing with Roger Kellaway and you need a radar machine to find the harmony sometimes, and we’re doing it at a jazz party.

ctx.x: I think I was one of the first guys to run an alto sax through a wa-wa pedal. And I had guys like Dave Holland in my band, and you know guys that just left Miles. I remember one time coming home and listening on the radio, and I was with a bass player, and I said, “Geez that sounds like us.” And it was Weather Report. This was back in the late ‘60s. So I was into that. I played with Dewey Redman and I played some avante garde music. These are experiences that to me I draw upon every time I get up to play. Because…

sudden if there’s a piano player who’s harmonically a little bit more advanced, okay, I can go here with this guy, you know. All of a sudden I know what I can do and what I can’t do. So each time is a very individual kind of situation and if you have all of these other experiences to draw from, you never run out of gas. I played with Vic Dickinson and Doc Cheatham, I played, you know Dixieland with these guys, I worked gigs with them. I mean they had their own thing going, their own humor, their own way of doing…
That’s something to pay attention to. That really is.
